content.title: What are JDK, JRE, and JVM?
content.description: JDK, JRE, and JVM are the three core components of the Java platform. Together, they enable developers to build, compile, and execute Java applications.

content.content: Many beginners confuse JDK, JRE, and JVM. Understanding their responsibilities is essential because every Java application depends on them. The JDK is used for development, the JRE provides the runtime environment, and the JVM executes Java bytecode.

content.title: Key Idea
content.content: JDK = Development Tools + JRE, JRE = JVM + Libraries, JVM = Executes Bytecode.
Each component has a different responsibility in the Java ecosystem.

items.question: What is JDK?
items.answer: Java Development Kit (JDK) is used by developers to write, compile, debug, and package Java applications.

items.question: What is JRE?
items.answer: Java Runtime Environment (JRE) provides the libraries and runtime environment required to execute Java programs.

items.question: What is JVM?
items.answer: Java Virtual Machine (JVM) converts bytecode into machine code and executes the program.

content.content: The JDK is the complete package required for Java development. It contains the compiler (javac), debugger, documentation tools, JRE, and other utilities needed to build Java applications.

content.title: Developer's Toolkit
content.description: If you want to create Java programs, you must install the JDK.

content.content: The JRE provides everything required to run Java applications. It includes the JVM and standard Java libraries but does not contain development tools like the compiler.

content.title: Remember
content.content: End users who only run Java applications need JRE, while developers require JDK.
The JVM is responsible for executing Java bytecode. It converts platform-independent bytecode into machine-specific instructions that the operating system can understand.
Java follows a two-step execution process. First, the compiler converts source code into bytecode. Then, the JVM converts the bytecode into machine code during execution.

content.title: Building and Driving a Car
content.content: Think of JDK as the car factory where vehicles are built. JRE is the road system that allows cars to operate, while the JVM is the engine that actually powers the car.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: The difference between JDK, JRE, and JVM is one of the most frequently asked Java interview questions.

items.question: Is JDK the same as JRE?
items.answer: No. JDK includes JRE along with development tools.

items.question: Does JVM compile Java code?
items.answer: No. The compiler (javac) in JDK compiles Java code into bytecode.

items.question: Can you develop Java applications using only JRE?
items.answer: No. You need the JDK because it provides the compiler and development tools.

content.title: Interview Tip
content.description: Remember the hierarchy: JDK contains JRE, and JRE contains JVM.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Platform independence is achieved through the JVM.
